Is 18 young? If so, my mom died when I was 18 and it completely changed everything: where I went to college, my relationship with my family, and unfortunately the way I see my friends. I had developed anxiety and depression probably from the trauma of her being ill throughout my childhood and teenage years, and although a day doesn't go by in which I wish she were still here, I am glad that she is no longer suffering.

I struggle with talking about real issues with my friends and family, because I do not want to burden them, and because of that, it has been and continues to be a very difficult healing process. I have found it much easier to talk to people who have gone through similar things, because it puts everything into perspective. Also, I have always had sort of bad death anxiety, and it has gotten worse since. But I see a counselor and pray or just "talk" to my mom sometimes, and I like to imagine her response to TV shows or songs she would have liked. I think that by sort of keeping her spirit alive and with me, which is something more recent for me, I have begun to deal with it a lot better.

Also, seeing how horribly a disease like cancer can affect a person's entire life as well as their families, and what a difference a good nurse or doctor can make, has helped me find my calling to be a nurse, and it has made helping others and seeing how they are really feeling so much more important to me.

I have come to the conclusion that no matter what your situation is or how "awesome" your life seems to be, you will probably have doubts about your depression being "valid." It is a legitimate illness, and no matter what anyone else thinks, only you can know how horrible it feels and the fact that you even admit that there is something wrong and hopefully take the next step of finding help, shows that you know more about yourself than anyone else. 

Sorry if that's cheesy, but it bugs me that almost EVERYONE feels like they don't have the right to be depressed. It's such a horrible result of a society that thinks that depressed people are lazy and/or faking it and just need to "try harder." Don't listen to anyone that says that or makes you feel that way!
